utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Ms. Pilipovic, is the Defence ready to continue to cross-examine -- to examine the Witness DP9?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Usher, could you please then escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. DP9.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP9, may I remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. Pilipovic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. DP9, good morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP9, yesterday, by the end of the sitting yesterday, you were asked if you knew if there were any damages on the church that you mentioned in the period 1992 to 1994, that there were certain operations around it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the spring and the summer of 1992 on the Orthodox church in Veljine there was some damages that were not so important made by hand-held rocket launchers and shells. And these weapons were fired on the church. I think that was in July. I believe it was July. But that period it's a bit difficult for me because it happened so long ago. But the church was quite damaged because of tank shells that were fired on it from the direction of Elo Elektra by the barracks Jusuf Dzonlic and then the former military rubbish dump. And as it was established in military expertise, the damage occurred because two tank shells -- first, it was one which was a tank and then the other one was of a different kind, they damaged the tower -- on the Veljine church.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. DP9. Mr. DP9 could you repeat the name of the barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that was Jusuf Dzonlic that was from that direction. I don't know whether that was left from the front to the back, but that was the part of town called Halilovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP9, do you have any knowledge at that time when you say that that you say from that barracks there was the firing of tanks. Who had the control of those barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the start of the hostilities these barracks was under the control of the Muslim army. At that moment, I don't know how they called themselves whether they were still the Green Berets or the Army of BH or I don't know what other name they used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP9, you told us yesterday where you were in the period of September 1992. You told us that you were a member of the Territorial Defence. Could you tell us in September 1992, what was the name of the military unit that you belonged to. Perhaps you mentioned it but could you perhaps repeat it just for continuity purposes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I belonged to the company which belonged to the 1st Infantry Battalion which was a part of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us your 1st battalion, which brigade did it belong?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it is possible that it was Ilidza Brigade because this area belonged to Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP9, could you tell us about the positions, the front lines and its length of your company, if you know, and of your battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that part of the front, my company held the line from the airport in Butmir, of the Krtelji base, Kotorac, Dobrinja, Dobrinja I, and for a while also of Dobrinja IV. And then in the continuation left and right the other companies' positions of this battalion continued.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP9, in your company, how many people, how strong was it, your company? Did your company contain smaller units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Companies are made up of platoons and the number of platoons vary but the base is about 110, 120 people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us as a member of the 1st Company of the 1st Battalion, you said there were about 100 of you. Your positions when we are speaking about being on duty, being on the front line, in which facilities did you have accommodation? What did you use?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depending on the configuration of the terrain and the facilities that were there, what we used were the buildings on the front lines, on the first lines, and where there were no buildings we used improvised trenches that we made on the sports airport. Down there, there were some containers which were reinforced to protect against fire. These were mostly the facilities that we used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, depending on the positions of your company, how far away was the front line, how far was the demarcation line between your company and the members of BH Army unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That also depended on the terrain that was between us. And it varied throughout the positions. It was mostly divided by streets and it could be a distance of about 20 or 50, sometimes 30 metres, and where there were less populated areas like the sports airport, civilian airport, there were -- there was much more distance between us, some 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to your -- the positions of your company, could you tell us in the period from September 1992 until the 10th of August 1994, was there combat in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this area, from time to time, there was combat. Sometimes fierce. There were fightings. I apologise. And during a certain period, and there were perhaps sometimes fighting of lesser intensity. Sometimes there was mutual firing and on a daily basis, and the firing was provoked sometimes by false alarms particularly during the time when there was not good visibility in early morning or in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP9, if the Defence presents you with a city plan, a city map, where you were as you say would you be capable of marking the lines, the positions of your company or battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know very well where the demarcation lines were.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your leave, the Defence would like to present part of the map that we have been using when we are examining witnesses. That would be Defence Exhibit D1770.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please assist.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP9, while we wait for the city map to be shown to you, could you tell us what kind of weapons did your company have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were an infantry unit, an infantry formation, and we had infantry weapons, which is supposed to be used by such formations. These were semi-automatic rifles, automatic rifles, grenades, hand-held rocket launchers. On the position of the company there was also a 60-millimetre mortar which as it was needed it was moved to where there were intense fighting or where there were direct threat of attack was reported to be. And we also used rifle grenades.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there a problem --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Computers are not working. It's okay now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, on the screen we cannot see the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP9, could you tell us, considering you told us about what weapons you used, what was your uniform like, if you had one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of the conflict we wore our own clothes except for people who at home -- except for people who at home as members of the reserve force had uniforms of the former Yugoslav Army and some people also had uniforms of the police reserve force which are of a different colour. But the uniforms we got later from an army warehouse and these were not complete uniforms, but in part. And I think that it was beginning of 1993 that I had the first complete new uniform and not an old one from a warehouse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP9, when you told us that on the part of the front line of your company there were fierce combat and shooting on a daily basis and firing from weapons, could you tell us whether you knew -- you had personal knowledge from which positions in relation to the positions of your company, units of the BH Army fired? Which were the positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the demarcation lines were so close, it wasn't hard to see where there was firing coming on to our positions, except that these points varied frequently, probably because of us returning the fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us from which weapons these units fired on your positions, and did they have some specific positions that you knew about and that were dominating your positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As an infantry soldier I knew the weapons quite well, so with a lot of accuracy I can say which weapons were used on the front lines. These were infantry weapons. Automatic rifles, semi-automatic rifles, hand-held grenade launchers. And from the Mojmilo hill one BST recoilless cannon. It's a type of artillery weapon. Then there were Browning heavy machine-guns. And then from the Igman elevation points, there were heavy artillery weapons, Howitzers, cannons and high-calibre mortars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now that you told us what weapons were used by the BH Army, you said BST. Could you please tell us what it is. Do we presume it to be a recoilless gun?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is a recoilless gun. It is an artillery weapon for shorter distances. I think it is most accurate, it is about 1.000, 1.500 metres. I am not an artillery man, so I don't know the exact characteristic of any medium character, but it is not a heavy weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you personally have knowledge from which positions this BST was fired?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were the positions of the Mojmilo hill which is located between the Dobrinja locality and the Alipasino Polje locality, and it dominates above one part of this locality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, I do see that the map is now on the ELMO and visible on our screens, so.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP9, could you have a look on your right-hand side and you have a map of the city. Could you perhaps mark on this map the positions --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Am I supposed to do it with a pencil?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With a very fine black liner, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you not to bend over that much because your head is in between the screen and -- yes. If you could do it this way.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I see, but it is a little small and I can't see that very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can, Mr. DP9, perhaps you can lift the map a little bit and move your hands.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this all right like this?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go a bit further up. I think that is okay. No, go a bit further up. The map. Could you just move it up so that we can see the lower part.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you see it now?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. This is okay now.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do I have to put in -- mark the positions of Republika Srpska Army?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP9, in relation to the line that you marked, marking the positions of your company, could you mark the positions, the front line of the BH Army in relation to yours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Am I supposed to do it with the same marker?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just with a dotted line, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please assist, because we cannot see it on the screen now. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP9, now that you have marked the positions with a dotted line, I can see that at one point this line is interrupted in the area of Donji Kotorac can you please explain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The interruptions of the line, as much as I was able to mark it on the map, represents the civilian airport which was under the control after UN forces, after they took it over from the Republika Srpska Army. And for a while, I don't know, later on it was taken over by SFOR and throughout the runway which was fenced off, they had their own vehicles and their own people there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP9, when you marked the lines on this map, the dotted lines as positions of the BH Army, could you tell us if you know what were the main facilities from which the BH Army was active, was operating, that they used on the first line of the front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the first line, residential buildings were used that were there and I marked in the position according to them. There is the school. At that time it was called Dusan Pajic-Dasic. I don't know what it is called now, because it belongs to the Federation now, so I don't know what the school is called now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP9, could you mark the position of this school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: How am I supposed to do that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just mark it with a number "1" and circle it with a pen.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number "1," yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what unit was located there? I am referring to the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to some information which mainly came from people who crossed over from the town or from people who were exchanged, the prisoners and detainees, I mean, there was a special unit there of members of the police commanded by a certain man called Vikic. He had been at that post before the a war but I don't know for how long they stayed there or how they changed shifts because there was some other positions there held by other units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say there were positions held by other units, could you be more precise? What units were they and what positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the school Dusan Pajic-Dasic they dug trenches in the direction of the Bijelo Polje road about 100 or 150 metres in front of the school where there were containers which had been left behind, which had been used as changing rooms for the sports area. There were also sandbags there. And there was a unit there which had arrived from the flank so as to be able to fire on the part of the area under our control. These were people who had dug the trenches and were later exchanged, and they knew that there were units from Dobrinja there and not Vikic's men. At the building and behind it, and the ground there is higher than the school itself there were firing points and I don't know who arranged this, but UN forces arrived to check on these. They came with APCs because these firing points were used to fire on the Bijelo Polje road which was an important communication.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP9, could you please mark the building that you say was behind the school building. Could you put a circle there and mark it with number "2."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This building I think has a ground floor and then six floors, and it is across the road from the school. I think that after the United Nations intervened, there was no firing from that position for a while -- for a time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP9, when you say that the UN intervened, can you tell us if you remember when this took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in the spring of 1994, but I am really sorry I can't be more precise. A lot of time has elapsed since then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. DP9. Today you told us, as far as I was able to understand, that two shells were fired from the Jusuf Dzonlic barracks in the direction of the church of Veljine. Can you mark on the map where this barracks was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that this was done from the direction of the barracks because there are some other military facilities around it. So I will put a circle but I can't pinpoint it with certainty. The people who carried out an on-site inspection when they were carrying out an inspection of the building marked it the way I will do now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP9, would you please mark this with a number "3."

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, this is in the area of the Jusuf Dzonlic barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DP9, you told us that shots were fired in the direction of the church. Can you tell us whether the church in Veljine was used for the purposes of the army of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Army of Republika Srpska had trenches in front of the church in Veljine and a prefabricated facility that had remained behind after the church was constructed. This was used to keep building materials in. And at the sides of the church in the wooded areas surrounding it, there were sentry posts. The church itself was not used for any military activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP9, when you spoke of the demarcation lines and marked them on the map, can you tell us whether there was any damage to residential buildings at the demarcation lines in that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Throughout the war as the buildings were where they were and as units of both armies were stationed there and there was constant firing, and because weapons were used in these activities, there was damage depending on the location of the building. Some buildings were damaged more; some less, depending on where they were and what extent they were exposed to the military activity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us as far as you know what parts of the buildings you used were damaged the most?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The buildings separating the Miroslava Krleze Street - I really don't know what it is called now - suffered the worst damage. So it was these buildings and the buildings across the road from them. Then the buildings in the Indira Gandhi Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP9, when you say -- what streets were the ones that were the most badly damaged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I show it on the map?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Should I just show it or mark it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You may just mark it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is these buildings here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you say this was the building -- the street called Miroslava Krleze Street.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a street that had two sides and the buildings were damaged on both sides, the same situation obtained in part of in the Indira Gandhi Street and I can't remember the other street names, but there is another street here which also was a street separating the right side from the left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you put a row of little X's there to show us where Miroslava Krleze Street and the Indira Gandhi Street where buildings were heavily damaged.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP9, can you tell us, since you spent some time there at the relevant time, 1992, 1993, 1994, can you tell us in your estimation whether the damage to the buildings was proportionate or was there more damage on one side than there was on the other? Can you assess this, you personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President. That calls for a legal conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When I heard the word "proportionate" the same thing came into my mind, but after I heard the explanation of Ms. Pilipovic, I think the question is admissible, so the objection is denied. So whether there was more damage on one side as there was on the other, that is what the question was. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So can you answer, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know to what extent I am able to estimate damage, but to me, in the places where there was an exchange of fire, furniture caught fire in the flats, and then the flats would burn. Where mortars landed, there was destruction of parts of walls. And it was the same on both sides of the lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP9, when you told us about your unit, can you tell us who the commander of your company was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My company commander was Mile Gavric. Before that in the beginning there was another man, his name was Zoran. I don't know what happened to him. He went elsewhere. He was there in the beginning and as a refugee. I didn't know the local population well. So I don't know whether he was a local man or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "local population" are you referring to the people who were in your company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my company, there were people who lived in that area but also others who, like me had fled from parts of town that were under Muslim control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether in your company there were professional soldiers or officers of the former JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my company there were no professional members of the Yugoslav Army, no officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how you as soldiers contacted your company commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wherever possible, temporary induction telephone lines were set up, provisional telephone lines. But where this was not possible, we used couriers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DP9, we talked about the buildings that were used at the front lines. Can you tell us whether there were civilians in those buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The buildings right next to the demarcation lines which were taken by the army on both sides there were no civilians. I am certain there were no civilians on our side. They were behind the lines in the rear. On the opposite side, I didn't see any civilians, and I assume they must have evacuated the civilians from buildings right along the demarcation line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say there were no civilians in the buildings, that they had been evacuated from the front line, can you tell us in particular in reference to the line -- the part of the line where your company was, what the depth at which the civilians were -- was? If you can show that on the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The civilians were, as far as buildings go, in these buildings here and in these buildings here, in family houses here. Their owners stayed in those houses. They were civilians. At this depth we also had our logistic support, food, telephone communications, first aid station in case someone was wounded. We controlled an area several hundred meters deep behind the front lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said you had first aid clinic in case someone was wounded, we are now referring to the part you marked. Can you tell us whether any civilians were wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This first aid station here was intended for soldiers. There were other outpatient clinics used for civilians and there were hospitals where civilians were taken. I wasn't there, but I know that if someone was wounded by a projectile, a projectile that went astray, perhaps, people had to have their wounds dressed and first aid had to be given them, and then they would be sent on for treatment.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, for the transcript, I want to say that the witness is explaining the position of the buildings between the line of separation and the place labelled "Bijelo Polje." So these are the buildings behind the demarcation line. Above the words "Bijelo Polje" in the lower part of the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DP9, you told us that members of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina fired from Mojmilo hill. Can you tell us what -- well, first of all, can you mark where these positions were, if you know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already marked this with a dotted line here facing the Starosjedoci area. These other slopes of Mojmilo and at higher elevation there were the weapons I mentioned, the recoilless gun, the Brownings and all this was here on this hill. There are family houses on the hill, trenches were dug connecting trenches and dugouts. And Atlantic City even higher elevation was the United Nations base which I think on one occasion during the war was taken by the Muslim army. But there were some members of the peacekeeping forces there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in view of the fact that the Defence has half an hour left, my colleague will use this time. My co-counsel will use this time to put some questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness. Thank you, Mr. President. Examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like us to come back to what you told us earlier. You told us about firing from tanks that hit the church. What parts of the church were hit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tower of the church was hit, of the Orthodox church in Veljine. Below the dome on the tower.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. With your own eyes, were you able to see this damage at the time; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just please answer with a yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you, yes or no, tell us what was the state of the tower, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean after the shelling?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the tank fired.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The front part of the tower facing Dobrinja and the other side facing Debelo Brdo were damaged, and the only thing that was left was the dome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as you know, was it possible to have access after the tower Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. was targeted? Was it possible to get to the higher point of the tower, to the higher part of the tower; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin did, I miss anything or as the witness not yet indicated where the church, the Veljine church was located?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, he gave the name of the church, and we are talking about the famous church which is located exactly at the corner of the square that he indicated, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, my question was, of course, since I mentioned the name of the church, you can deduce of that, that I heard the witness use the name. When I asked whether the witness indicated already where the church was located, it is not to you to say where the church was located, but you can ask the witness whether he could indicate where the church was located. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please use the pointer or even your hand and just to indicate on the map where the church that we are talking is located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness pointed to the church located on the map which is just the angle of the corner of the square that he drew on the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, what could you do so that it is clearer, could you please place number "4" next to the church. "5." I think we have already had 4.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, why -- why wasn't it possible to get to the upper part of the tower?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the building itself, there are no steps that lead to the dome or to the tower. You only go with steps to the bell. But there were some exits and some covers, and those people who came after the church was damaged, they said that these exits and openings were just covered by the debris after the shelling, and people couldn't get to the tower any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, what you are saying is that part of the wall fell down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to go to another subject now since we have the map of the city in front of us. First of all, I would like to ask you to take the pointer, please, thank you, and to place it on the northern part of the line that you drew alongside the street that was known as Lukavica Street.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Could you just move your pointer to the left, please. And by following the street -- no. Go by the main road on the left. Yes, a little bit further. Stop now. Stop now. In the area that you just indicated, Witness, do you know if there was just one single system of trenches, I am talking about the trenches of the opposing side, or were there several? And I am talking about the segment that you just indicated.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this part that Lukavicka Cesta was dug up so that it can be used as a trench, as a connecting trench for communication towards the buildings of Dobrinja going towards this side, and towards the Mojmilo hill. Just behind the road, there were these trenches, connecting trenches to which manpower and supplies came. And then there was another system of trenches which went towards this side of the water supply towards the top of Mojmilo hill where there was a passage to the Mojmilo locality and Alipasino locality. And there was another trench which runs through the fields and orchards up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. As far as you know, I would like you to take again the fine liner, and if you can please draw this on the map as accurately as possible. Thank you. And please by using dotted lines.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, thank you. Could you just place your pen to the beginning of the line or the lines that you drew. You just drew another line. Could you please place your pen there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness is pointing to the south of the lines that he drew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is this location? Do you know what is there, what is located there to the south of the road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this location, on the left-hand side there is the electricity transmitter for the Dobrinja. There is some green area and then all the way to the Lamela building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. I think that I heard --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I heard, Mr. President, that there was talk of the parking which I cannot see that in the translation, that is, I cannot see it in the transcript. And since I heard the parking mentioned, I am going to ask a question again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I believe that you mentioned a parking. Was it a mistake? Did I have a dream?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There are several parking lots there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but I am only interested in one and it is not in the transcript. Could you please indicate this parking, Witness, please. This is deliberate, I know that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I noticed that you are speaking aloud in a language that we cannot hear. And I heard the translators saying something like "this is deliberate." Was that a translation of what Mr. Piletta-Zanin --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Indeed, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, what, if you are talking to Ms. Pilipovic, we now notice that this is translated as well. I don't know what was deliberate or not deliberate, but I asked you before not to speak at such a tone that anyone else could hear it, if you confer between counsel. Would you please keep that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Mr. President. I apologise most profusely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please indicate again the location of this parking lot please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I understand this map, it is this, this and this. All of these are parking lots between the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, the witness mentioned several parkings which are to the south of the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in relation to this, what we are talking about, what was the distance in relation to this parking lot that we are talking about? Could you tell us what was the distance between the parking lot itself and the nearest trenches that you drew, if you know that approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a green area to where the trenches where, between there and where the trenches are. It could be --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I am sorry. The interpreter didn't hear the number of metres of the distance. Could the witness please repeat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the number of metres you just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Between 40 and 50 metres. It is one green area. It is a green, which is next to the parking lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Witness, from the positions that you had the control of that you occupied, and if you know from the Lukavica barracks, was it possible to see the parking lot that we just spoke about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, that is impossible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, Witness, I am going to go to another line of questioning. You indicated -- this is a very last question -- did you know if these trenches that you just drew were used by the army, by the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for their needs. They dug them -- they dug them for their needs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would now like to go to another line of questioning, Witness. You spoke of a mortar, a 60-millimetre mortar. Did you have the opportunity to find out about even theoretically something about the way this weapon functioned; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know if this type of weapon is a very accurate weapon; yes or no? Do you know that? What can you tell us about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a weapon, there are many reasons whether it is accurate or not depends on who is handling it, whether this person is trained or not, and what kind of ammunition is used, whether it is old ammunition, whether it was used provisionally, whether it was changed, modified, and every weapon has a margin of error, which it makes when it is used, when it is being operated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have some problems in receiving the French translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am on another channel so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I am on the English channel. Could we just see whether we receive any French translation on channel 5. We do not. Is there a technical problem? We do not get any translation on channel 5 in French. Is there -- is it the interpreters that have problems or are the technicians --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear us in the English channel?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... a technical problem to be solved.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. President, just one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The French booth is now speaking on the English channel to ask if we can hear them and clearly they are coming through on that channel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I now switched to channel 4. Yes, I hear -- [Interpretation] At the moment, I am listening to you on number 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much and thank you for the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now Witness, you told us earlier about the area at the back where civilians still lived. Could you please indicate it on the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be about here, is where the buildings are concerned, but this and that over there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness indicated two areas to the north and south of the enclave next to number "5."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, these two areas that we have, were there, as far as you know, shellings that took place? If yes, what were they like and where did they come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These areas suffered shellings on several occasions with heavy weapons and mortars from Mount Igman and from the direction of the city of Sarajevo. I think from the area of Alipasino Polje with heavy mortars and with lighter mortars from the area of Mojmilo and from the area of Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Were there military targets there as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the areas on the edges there was part of the military logistics. There were kitchens and the clinic, as I have already said. And further at the back in some parts was the former barracks. In the other parts there was nothing else except private houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, how could you explain this firing, therefore, this targeting of these areas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well I presume that the civilian areas were not the actual targets of this artillery but these projectiles were probably badly fired. They were of poor quality or simply the weapons, the charges were not of good quality and they probably didn't fall where they were supposed to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as you know, what you're telling us were mistakes. Was this frequent, very frequent, relatively frequent? How would you describe this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we are talking about people who are not so well trained to handle weapons, and because these were old storages of ammunition. These were war reserves from the 50s and the 60s and because they were also improvised, made new workshops with poor charges, this was a frequent occurrence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the assistance of Madam Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Registrar, I will show you Exhibit 3274, P3274 with the ERN number 02 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, if this will help you, we have the photo itself, just to save time, if we can have your permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We could use that photograph and then see whether Madam Registrar finds the original, we can compare it. She has found it already so perhaps we better use the original. Did you indicate before Mr. Piletta-Zanin, to Madam Registrar, that you would use this photograph? That would be very helpful so that she can prepare for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, and I apologise for that. Because I have to do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If would also be helpful if advance notice could be given to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is examination-in-chief so you could have foreseen that you were going to use this photograph, and it would have been fair to inform the Prosecution as well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3274 has A, B, C. Which photograph would you like, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's the B, the one that I showed you. Thank you, in advance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you prefer to use the marked or the unmarked photograph? And would the Prosecution oppose against the unmarked?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The marked photo would save us time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If I could see the photograph, please, then, the marked one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please put the photograph on the ELMO, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In such a way that we don't have the reflection. Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, just for the record, this appears to relate to a sniping incident that is not part of the Rule 65 ter or expanded Rule 65 ter notice that the Defence has provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, is this either 6 or 18?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Here we are going to speak about the incident number 22 on one hand, and of another matter more important as a general rule, which is the quality of the maps that is submitted to us. The questions are to be asked -- must be asked in order to find out whether what has been shown to us on Prosecution maps, whether this is to be trusted or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where do we find this in your 65 ter summary?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not sure that we can find it in this form, but I think this is going to be a matter of principle. We always maintained that we will try and demonstrate that these maps which are purely virtual, they are contested by the Defence. And we didn't think it was necessary to put it in writing but from now on, we can should be more extensive. This is a principle. We are contesting these maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am not contesting your right to contest maps. But I am just point at your duty to indicate what the witness will testify about and if it is about the inaccuracy of maps, it should be in the 65 ter. And if you want to pay attention to incident number 22, it is at least surprising that if you mention two other incidents, that you do not indicate that it is also about 22. That is -- the matter of principle of course no one denies the Defence the right to contest the accuracy of maps. But that is not the issue. The issue is whether the Prosecution could prepare for cross-examination by having a reliable basis in your 65 ter summary. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, for the record, the Prosecution also objects to the colloquy on page 28, lines 17 through 23, having taken place in the presence of the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps I should have been more cautious in this respect as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, bearing in mind the cooperation of the parties we suggest to pass on to incident number 6 which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... the Judges are conferring so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the reason why what you want to ask the witness is not in the 65 ter summary is not an acceptable reason. We will let you continue now, but this is not a decision on whether we will take into consideration the evidence that follows from it, and the Chamber will consider how to proceed when this happens again. It is not the first time. You have been invited to be more precise. What we see now is that you leave out whole sniping incidents that you think are relevant. We will keep a close eye on what kind of questions you are going to put to the witness now. We will also keep in mind whether these questions are such that it would be really -- whether it really would have frustrated the Prosecution's preparation for cross-examination. But I indicate already to you that we cannot proceed this way. I hope, and the Chamber is not willing to repeat these kind of remarks for the next eight weeks. So just saying, "well I should have done it or I should not have done it, it is a matter of principle, we denied it so many times." We, the Chamber, wants just as the Defence should have and usually had a fair opportunity to prepare for cross-examination, the same is valid for the Prosecution. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the photograph that you can see on your right, Witness, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And perhaps could we have a zoom on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you see what is mentioned to the side of the arrow which is in the centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please zoom on the arrow. Could we go to the maximum, please. I presume this is the maximum.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, what you have just below the arrow, what is it, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are buildings, private houses, that are part of the so-called airport settlement, airport locality, next to Dobrinja V.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Nothing else? Could you tell us something else? Could you see anything else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is where the arrow is pointing, on the right and left-hand side are the buildings in continuation of the Mitsubishi Avenue. There are some restaurants there, some disco clubs. I know this area quite well because that is where I live.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can remove the photograph now. I would like to have another map shown referring to incident number 6 which I believe was clearly mentioned in our summary and bears the number of 1771. I think this map should be placed on the ELMO. But, Mr. President, I believe that we are approaching breaktime and I don't know whether it would be a good idea to have a break now and then we can continue with the questions after. Whatever you want.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time would you still need, Mr. Piletta-Zanin? Because I notice that at five minutes to --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Some time, Mr. President, because we have to be very precise on these incidents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time I asked you, that it will be a certain time that -- because Ms. Pilipovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quarter of an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because Ms. Pilipovic told us that at five minutes to 10.00 that since you would have another half an hour, I think she was rather moderate, because you had more time. So, therefore, yesterday you took 20 minutes. Today you used one hour and 25 minutes. So that would mean that you have one quarter of an hour left. We will adjourn until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, I have a few remarks to make. The first is that unfortunately - and I inform the Defence right away - that for technical reasons it seems not to be possible to have the videolink as scheduled. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, as far as I understand by now that the videolink could be established on from the 12th of November. I think it was scheduled to start next Monday, but it will be the Tuesday in the week to follow next week. So that would be the 12th of November where we could start. The Chamber regrets that it cannot be done as scheduled, but technical difficulties, we can do a lot, but not to solve the technicians' problems and the availability of people. So, therefore, please prepare for the 12th of November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there would be objections, for example, for reasons of the availability of the witnesses, please inform the Registry as soon as possible so that final arrangements can be made. As long as we do not hear from you, we take it that the witnesses will be available on the 12th of November and if necessary the following day. Then the second issue I would like to address is that we have experienced several times, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that when you hear something in the original language of the witness, and if you notice it has not been part of the translation, you, at several occasions, indicated what you heard in the original language and that it was not in the translation. Under these circumstances, it would be proper to ask the witness without any further explanation to repeat his answer and perhaps ask specific attention of the interpreters, since you missed, and there is no problem if you say, "I missed something in the translation." But you should not tell in the presence of the witnesses what part you did not hear in the translation and what, as you heard it, was part of his answer. So under the circumstances, indicate that there might be an incomplete translation, and invite the witness to repeat his answer and then the interpreters, I am certain, it's -- I mean, if a mistake is made, the interpreters are not the only ones in the world who would make a mistake. I am very impressed by the performances and just as we all make mistakes, it might happen, but then we should ask the witness to repeat his answer and the interpreters then will be fully aware to even do even more their best, as they already do. Then the third issue is about the 65 ter summaries. This morning there was a complaint, and I think the complaint was justified, and I don't know what else we will hear, what testimony we will hear about incident 22. If it would just be what we heard until now, it might not have a dramatic effect. But the Chamber uses this opportunity to make clear that the Defence is entitled to examine witnesses in order to present its case. But the Rules are quite clear whether you repeated certain issues already seven or eight or nine times is of no importance. The Prosecution should know what they can expect and should be in a position to prepare for cross-examination. It's not the first time now that this has happened and as you might have -- as you all know that in football matches, those referees that are very lenient in the beginning, at a certain moment they will pull a yellow card and you know what comes after the yellow card. The Defence is entitled, but to examine witnesses, it is a fundamental right, but it is not a right that can be exercised without observing duties attached to it. And one of the duties is that the Defence should give such 65 ter summaries that the Prosecution is in a position to prepare for cross-examination. I hope that this is a clear position. Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Given those comments, this might be an appropriate time to draw to your attention a filing by the Defence yesterday which expresses itself to be in accordance to the decision of the Trial Chamber. The filing is described as "the broader Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. summaries of statements of the witnesses," in other words, the expanded 65 ter summaries. I notice that the summaries appear to still not comply with the oral order of the Trial Chamber last week. Could I draw your attention for example, to witness number 21 - I won't give the witness's name - the last sentence of that summary reads: "His testimony would be important for scheduled sniping incidents numbers 4, 9 and 14," and nothing more is said. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will read it. If that would be the last sentence, then it does not comply with the order. Mr. Piletta-Zanin you have another 15 minutes to examine in chief the witness. Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much for your decision, Mr. President. I take note of the opinion. I take it to be a red card, if I understood your words correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, the red card is what will come if you continue to do similar things. Please be seated, Mr. DP9. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning again, Witness. I don't know whether what we have on the screen -- could we just check that. Yes. Thank you. Witness, having looked at the map on your right, could you please look at the document, 3264, which I have here, which was mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have got a copy, if that can save time.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I am sorry, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. I don't know which document you are referring to. It is a "P" document or...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that the copies you just distributed or...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I just asked for your leave to show the witness document P3264. I have a copy in my hand, and if it is in the interest of saving time, then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you -- have you indicated this to the Registrar during the break, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mentioned it on the list, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is on the last list?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the list 14th through the 18th of October, 2002. And I don't know whether -- it is the very last page, in any case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please show it to the Prosecution, whether there would be any -- is this a marked photograph or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It is marked in a sense that there are some pen markings on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you put it on the ELMO so that you can see it. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, this exhibit was notified to us by the Defence and we have our copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When was this done? Last --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I believe on the 11th of October.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then please put it on the ELMO. Yes, we could use a photo for the time being, a copy, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. I take it that the Prosecution will carefully see to it that it is the same document. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise this photograph, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, can you distinguish something which seems to be like the bell tower of the church? It is slightly to the left.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Behind this building I see a dome of the Orthodox church in Veljine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, bearing in mind or referring to the item that you have described --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I am listening. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, is this the facility which was reconstructed after the tank firing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This facility was reconstructed only after the Dayton Agreement. I think in 1996, and throughout the war, this facility was destroyed and it was not possible to restore it or rebuild it because of the firing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. This type of photograph with the outline of the church that we can see, could it have been taken, bearing in mind the destruction in this way precisely, at the time of the war after the shelling of the church; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the photograph, please-- Mr. Usher, could you please -- [In English] Could we have the map on the ELMO. [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at this map on your right, Witness, could you please identify with the pointer two points where there is number "6" and where there is number "18." Do you see them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is point number "6" and point number "18."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, the witness did as he was asked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the question I want to ask you is the following: From what we call the site of the church, Witness, do we have any kind of direct view on the canal of the Dobrinja, and what I mean by the site of the church is the front of the church.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Prosecution objects unless it can be established that the witness was in the church and had a line of sight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please verify the factual basis of the knowledge of the witness, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the front doesn't mean the -- inside the church. And what I mean for the French transcript that I am listening, and the interpretation that I am listening is not what appears in the English transcript.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, did you go at the time, at the time of the war, to the location of the church that we are talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you go to the front of the church, that is, the clearing which is located in front of the main entrance to the church?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever look from that location towards Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And now I am just going to ask you: Did you go to the Lukavica Barracks; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, since you went to the front of the church and turned towards Dobrinja, since you went there, did you see, did you have a direct view on the Dobrinja river; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The view of the Dobrinja river is hidden by a wooded area, by tall buildings that were constructed in Dobrinja IV and III.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it possible, Witness, at any point in the war to see in front of the square in front of the church, the front of the church, was it possible to see the water in the Dobrinja river?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, now, starting from the principle that assuming that the church has not changed location, did you go back after the war to the church on whatever occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I go to church regularly when there are important church holidays.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever have the opportunity to go to this church, to the upper floor of this church, if it is possible to go there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The access is possible only to the first balcony of the church where the choir is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am going to stop you here. From this first balcony of the church did you ever look to the outside in the direction of Dobrinja, if there is an opening, if there is an opening to look through?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a small church window on the balcony. It is made of a coloured glass, invitrage, so you cannot look from the church outside. It is about 4 metres up from the level of the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I am going to come back to the photograph that you had a look at and that you identified. At the time of the events and bearing in mind, Witness, what you just told us, would it have been technically possible for a shot to be fired from the location of the church and hit someone on the road that you see before you? Do you want me to repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us why not, according to you, technically speaking, it is not possible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that the tower was shelled and even if it was possible to get up there, this was exposed to firing from all the surrounding buildings and Mojmilo hill, and this would have been equal to suicide to attempt such a thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, you told us that you also went to the Lukavica Barracks. From the Lukavica Barracks, did you ever have a look at in the direction of Dobrinja; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it possible from the Lukavica Barracks to look to see beyond the very front line the first line, the Serb line in Dobrinja, is it possible to see beyond there; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, was it possible from the Serb lines that you indicated whether they were on the front line or at the rear, was it possible to see the sight of the parking lot that you indicated earlier which is located 40 or 50 metres from the trenches of the defence; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You categorically claim "no"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The parking lot is surrounded by tall buildings, by three -- on three sides, and the fourth side is the Mojmilo hill which we did not have under our control, so we were not able to see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The very last question, Witness. On the map that you have on your right, you see the lines that go down in an oblique way north-east, south-west. Can you see these defence lines going in that direction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean these lines?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Could you continue these lines. These lines, yes. Thank you very much. These lines, bearing in mind in what you have just told us, do these lines seem correctly indicated or incorrectly indicated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a small part they are correct, but for the most part they are not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please indicate the areas that are not -- that have not been correctly marked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is incorrect is the line or put too far back. This is the Miroslava Krleze Street. Next to the school, that is completely wrongly put in. It is in fact a completely different direction. It is an error of about half a kilometre, more than half a kilometre. Here this is correct, and this part here is -- this is small map -- but this may be 10 metres or so where there is a mistake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, as much as you can with a black pen, could you please mark, indicate again, what you think to be the true line of the Serb lines, please, with a black pen.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. This is referring to Serb lines; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please mark next to them -- could you please mark next to them indication like "VRS" or "SRK" at the bottom of the line. Put "SRK," bottom of the line, yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And if on this map, if you can also rectify the other line, the opposing line, the positions of the other side, if this is possible could you do that, in a dotted line, please. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Witness, I would like us to move on the map and to look on the other side, the western side below the -- no, above, above the central boulevard of Dobrinja. Could we please move the map on the ELMO slightly. Thank you. Stop, stop, stop. Above where it says "boulevard" you see long buildings. Could you please indicate just above the word "boulevard." I think that is the Boulevard of the Defenders. To the left. More to the left. No, that's right. Please, to the left. To the left. No. No. Above. Above. Yes. Stop. No, above. Above. Yes. Don't move.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, the witness is pointing to a rectangle representing a building, and I think that is -- this is above the word "boulevard."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Now, how high was this building, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This building is located in the former Mitsubishi Avenue where there are many shops and commercial centres and I think that this building has eight to ten floors. I can't remember exactly at the moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Building that are around to the south, south-west, and to the north-west of these buildings, are these buildings of the same height?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These buildings are of similar height, perhaps there is a floor of difference between them. I can't exactly tell you. But this is approximately the height. This is a locality which was built in staircase.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very last question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, this really is the last question. You took already 80 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you know if there were prisons in Dobrinja, and if yes could you indicate their name and location, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what I know from the exchanges and people who have escaped, there were at least two prisons in the former discotheque Turbo Mitsubishi and in the Babylon discotheque and these were in the underground premises of these buildings and one of the prisons was called Sunce.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you tell us where prisons appear in the 65 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have it before me. I can't give you an answer now. At these elements which were just handed to me. I don't know -- I don't have it here on this very spot. Perhaps I could check and let you know a little later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the Prosecution ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Cross-examined by Mr. Mundis:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, DP9.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us when the first time you met with the Defence counsel in this case, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well I think it was in the spring that I had contacts with some people, a gentleman and a lady, who came to ask me whether I would be willing to testify in this trial.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These people that you are referring to, this gentleman and lady, were they investigators or were they the Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were counsel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see either of those counsel in the courtroom today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not the ones I saw then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "it was in the spring" was that the spring of 2002?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was in the spring of this year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you met with this gentleman and this lady, did you tell them about the confrontation lines or the demarcation lines that you've testified about today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't discuss those matters. They simply wanted some information as to whether I would be willing to appear before The Hague Tribunal, if it was necessary. And they wanted to take my details so that if I agreed to testify, they could keep me informed of further developments. They told me that I might be called upon to testify quite soon, perhaps in May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
